item.title: Chasing twilight at Arial Beel
item.description:
When it comes to rich wetland biodiversity, Bangladesh stands as a classic example of a delta blessed with numerous beels and haors. These vast landscapes act as an economic lifeline for millions of rural farming, fishing, and boatmen communities.
Over the years, I have visited many of these wetlands, but I had always missed Arial Beel—the country's third-largest beel , covering 136 square kilometers and located just an hour's drive south of Dhaka.
A recent autumn trip to Munshiganj’s Sreenagar finally brought me to this massive wetland.
Behind the writer stretches a serene landscape of Arial Beel, a vast wetland bathed in the warm, golden hues of a setting sun. The calm, glassy waters perfectly mirror the soft, hazy sky, where the sun hangs low on the distant horizon like a distinct, glowing orb—casting a peaceful evening ambiance over the entire scene. Photo: Dhaka Tribune/Collected
Approaching a vantage point that offered a 360-degree view of the marshland, I encountered minivans heading in the opposite direction. They were loaded with water lilies harvested since early morning by local farmers, who collect them from boats to sell as a popular regional vegetable.
I was heading toward Gadighat, a primary gateway for travelers. By the time I reached the concrete Gadighat Bridge (locally also known as Tuta Bridge), twilight had already arrived. With its elevated concrete railings stretching across the canal docks, the bridge serves as the ultimate open-air viewing deck.
The timing was flawless. The retreating sun cast deep crimson hues across the horizon, while the sprawling, mirror-like waters below perfectly reflected the glowing evening sky.
An aerial lens captures Tuta Bridge (Gadighat Bridge) cutting across the expansive waterways of Arial Beel. Flooded by monsoon and post-monsoon waters, the entire wetland becomes a sea of emerald green, carpeted in water hyacinths and lily pads. This essential crossing arches over the central canal, tying together the rural fields and communities of Tuta and Gadighat. Photo: Dhaka Tribune/Collected
Because it was the post-monsoon season, the water levels had begun to recede. While the height of the rainy season surely turns Arial Beel into an endless sea of lilies and isolated, island-like villages, the receding water is a different kind of blessing.
As the dry winter months approach, local farming communities take advantage of the fertile, exposed soil. This is when farmers sow seeds for sweet pumpkins, which Arial Beel is famous for. Cultivated in Munshiganj’s rich wetland soil, these massive, ribbed squashes easily weigh a hefty 10 and 30 kilograms. Local lore holds that Arial Beel regularly breaks records with single pumpkins tipping the scales at over 100 kilograms! From here, boats and trucks ship these giants en masse to feed the bustling markets of Dhaka.
Standing with hands clasped, the writer leans gently against a red-and-white striped roadside guide post. Positioned on a concrete bridge, this elevated vantage point offers a panoramic view of the sunset painting the sprawling marshland below. Photo: Dhaka Tribune/Collected
Beyond agriculture, Arial Beel is a treasure trove of ecological biodiversity, serving as a vital resting and foraging ground for migratory ducks and diverse bird populations. Topographically, a beel is a large, saucer-shaped depression that accumulates rainwater, runoff, and river overflow. Unlike moving rivers or canals, beels feature relatively static freshwater.
Bangladesh is home to several other prominent beel ecosystems:
Chalan Beel: Located across Rajshahi, Pabna, Sirajganj, and Natore, it is Bangladesh’s largest beel . It transforms into an endless inland sea during the monsoons and a patchwork of rice and mustard fields in the winter.
Beel Dakatia: Situated in Khulna and Jessore, this is the country's second-largest beel , functioning as a major tidal deltaic wetland and aquaculture hub.
This traditional climate-adaptive method of floating agriculture (Dhap) thrives along the interior floodplains and natural canals of Arial Beel. The beds are securely anchored in the calm, deep depressions locally called dengas, where the current won’t sweep the floating structures away. Photo: Dhaka Tribune/Collected
Baikka Beel: Falling within the Hail Haor ecosystem in Moulvibazar, this protected fish and bird sanctuary is one of the premier spots in the country for birdwatching.
Satla Beel: Located in Barisal, it is celebrated as an iconic "kingdom of water lilies" that draws extensive regional tourism.
As I wrapped up my visit and the sun dipped below the horizon, I reflected on how these wetlands sustain local livelihoods. From fishing and foraging lilies to cultivating giant pumpkins and utilizing traditional, climate-adaptive floating agriculture (Dhap) in calm depressions known as dengas , the ecosystem is highly productive.
Arial Beel is famous for its abundant sweet pumpkin harvests. Cultivated in Munshiganj’s rich wetland soil after the monsoons recede, these massive, ribbed squashes are shipped en masse to major kitchen markets across Dhaka. Photo: Dhaka Tribune/Collected
However, as I departed, it was impossible to ignore how urbanization is slowly but surely creeping into the edges of the wetland. For the sake of both nature and the communities that rely on it, this encroachment needs to stop.

item.title: India silent on Hasina return conditions, says extradition ‘a legal matter’
item.description:
India on Friday reiterated that it desires a “positive, constructive and forward-looking” relationship with Bangladesh but refrained from commenting specifically on a BBC Bangla report claiming that New Delhi had set two conditions for facilitating former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s possible return to Bangladesh in December this year.
India also referred to the matter of Hasina’s extradition as a legal issue.
“So what I refer to as a legal matter was the extradition part. Extradition is a legal matter, and it will be dealt with accordingly,” Indian Ministry of External Affairs Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told reporters at a regular briefing in New Delhi.
Journalists drew his attention to the report suggesting that New Delhi wants Bangladesh to send a military aircraft to bring Sheikh Hasina back from India and has sought assurances that she would be given an opportunity to appeal her death sentence and face a fresh trial. The spokesperson, however, made no specific comments on the report.
According to the BBC Bangla report, New Delhi has identified two principal conditions for facilitating Hasina’s return to Bangladesh.
The first is that the Bangladesh Army must take responsibility for bringing her back, preferably using a military aircraft, as she originally arrived in India aboard a Bangladesh military aircraft after fleeing the country on August 5, 2024.
The second condition is that Bangladesh must guarantee Hasina an opportunity to appeal her death sentence and undergo a fresh trial over allegations relating to the July 2024 killings.
The report said Hasina’s continued presence in India has increasingly become an embarrassing issue for the Indian government, both in its bilateral relations with Bangladesh and on the international stage.
Asked about the postponement of the consular dialogue between Bangladesh and India, Jaiswal said India desires a “positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship” with Bangladesh. Accordingly, he said, initiatives have been taken and meetings held under structured mechanisms in areas such as trade, railways, water resources and border management, among others.
Jaiswal said the next round of consular dialogue, which will also take up matters relating to the revised travel arrangement, would be held on a mutually convenient date.
“India remains ready to discuss all matters or all bilateral issues with Bangladesh through these existing mechanisms, including at the technical level. So, the consular dialogue will be held at a mutually convenient date,” he said.
Bangladesh and India have more than 40 bilateral mechanisms covering issues including water, trade, border management and consular affairs, an official told UNB.
The two countries were discussing holding the fifth consular dialogue in Dhaka later this month (November 17-18), but a diplomatic source told UNB on Monday that the meeting would not take place as scheduled.
Minister (Press) at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi Saidur Rahman on Thursday said the consular dialogue had been postponed a week before the request concerning former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s passport and national identity card was submitted.
“I can state with certainty that the decision to postpone the dialogue was made at least four days before the request for a passport and national ID on behalf of Sheikh Hasina was submitted on November 9. This has absolutely nothing to do with any announcement regarding Sheikh Hasina’s potential return to the country,” he said.
The Bangladesh-India consular dialogue mechanism was instituted in 2017 to strengthen people-to-people contacts by establishing a regular channel of communication on consular, visa and mutual legal assistance cooperation matters between the two countries.
An inter-ministerial meeting was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka on November 3 as part of preparations for the consular dialogue. The dialogue was expected to discuss cross-border issues, border management, streamlining visa processes, repatriating citizens detained in either country, securing the release and repatriation of fishermen, and promoting mutual legal cooperation.
The fourth round of consular dialogue was held on May 29, 2024, in New Delhi. The two sides held wide-ranging discussions on mechanisms to strengthen coordination and cooperation on consular issues, visa matters, repatriation, MLAT and extradition cases, among others. They also agreed to further strengthen the bilateral Revised Travel Arrangement (RTA) to facilitate the movement of nationals between the two countries.
Both sides reiterated their commitment to promoting people-to-people exchanges and agreed to hold the next round of dialogue in Dhaka on a mutually convenient date.
Meanwhile, longstanding water-sharing disputes and emerging challenges in transboundary water management are becoming increasingly pressing.
Jaiswal recently said India was ready to discuss all bilateral issues with Bangladesh through the existing structured mechanisms.
On the Ganga Water Treaty, the MEA spokesperson said on November 3 that the two countries have a Joint Rivers Commission.
“That is the structured mechanism for discussion on all cross-boundary rivers, including the Ganga. As far as any further development in that regard is concerned, I have no update to share with you.”
With the Ganga Water Treaty approaching expiry in December, Bangladesh faces the task of securing an equitable and sustainable water-sharing arrangement while strengthening cooperation on other shared rivers.

item.title: Air travel tops 10m passengers in first six months
item.description:
Air travel in Bangladesh is growing rapidly, with more than 10.31 million passengers using the country's eight airports in the first six months of 2026, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB).
Passenger traffic increased by 5.41% in 2025 compared to the previous year, while the latest figures indicate continued growth in both domestic and international travel.
CAAB spokesperson and Assistant Director Muhammad Kawsar Mahmud said airlines operating international flights are being encouraged to use Shah Amanat and Osmani international airports to ease pressure on Dhaka's Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
He said both airports have adequate facilities for international operations. CAAB is also working to distribute flight schedules more evenly throughout the day to prevent congestion during peak hours.
According to CAAB data, the country's airports handled 16.67 million passengers in 2024, rising to 17.57 million in 2025. The increase amounted to around 901,000 passengers in a year.
Of the 10.31 million passengers recorded in January-June this year, 7.94 million travelled internationally and 2.37 million domestically.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport handled 8.52 million passengers during the first six months of 2026, accounting for around 82.7% of the country's total air traffic.
The figure is already higher than the airport's stated annual passenger-handling capacity of around eight million.
Of the passengers using Shahjalal during the period, 7.34 million were international travellers and 1.18 million domestic passengers.
The airport handled 13.12 million passengers in 2024, rising to 13.86 million in 2025, a year-on-year increase of 5.64%.
The growing passenger volume is putting pressure on immigration, security checks, boarding, baggage handling, aircraft parking and ground services, often causing delays and inconvenience.
The pressure is not limited to passengers, as large numbers of visitors also gather at airports to receive or see off travellers, adding to congestion in terminal areas.
Passenger traffic is also increasing at regional airports, particularly in Sylhet and Cox's Bazar.
Osmani International Airport handled 748,039 passengers in 2024 and 887,385 in 2025, recording 18.63% growth. It served 479,608 passengers in the first six months of 2026.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Cox's Bazar Airport recorded an 18.36% increase in passenger traffic in 2025, rising from 558,704 in 2024 to 661,283. It handled 364,920 passengers during January-June this year.
During the same six-month period, Shah Amanat International Airport in Chittagong handled 716,897 passengers, while Saidpur recorded 152,257, Rajshahi 43,593, Jessore 24,197 and Barisal 6,366.
Former CAAB chairman Air Vice Marshal (retd) M Mofidur Rahman said passenger numbers had been rising since 2019, but infrastructure and operational capacity had not expanded at the same pace.
He said several projects had been undertaken to expand airports in Dhaka, Chittagong, Sylhet and Cox's Bazar, but progress had not been sufficient.
The government has taken various initiatives, he said, adding that effective implementation and improved management would be essential to address the growing pressure.
He also stressed the need for the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism to give greater attention to upgrading existing infrastructure and operational capacity.
Kamrul Islam, general manager of public relations at private airline US-Bangla Airlines, said rising passenger numbers were encouraging for the aviation industry.
However, he said authorities needed to address existing challenges to ensure the sector's further development.
Industry experts say sustained growth in passenger traffic could strengthen domestic airlines, but inadequate airport infrastructure and services may undermine the sector's ability to accommodate rising demand.

item.title: Armed gang robs 8 RU students in Garo hills
item.description:
Eight students of Rajshahi University (RU) were allegedly held at gunpoint, assaulted and robbed while visiting the Garo hills in Jhenaigati Upazila of Sherpur on Friday morning.
The incident took place around 9am at a hill near the Gazni Abokash tourist centre, reports Bangla Tribune.
The students said a group of armed men, carrying a pistol and locally made sharp weapons, held them captive and tied them up before beating them and snatching their mobile phones, wallets and cash.
Rimon Rayhan, a student of the university's Department of Social Work, said 73 students had travelled from Rajshahi University to visit the tourist centre and split into several groups to explore the surrounding hills.
An eight-member group was attacked after climbing a nearby hill, he said. The attackers fled with their belongings, after which the victims returned to the tourist centre and reunited with their companions with help from locals.
Gazni tourist centre caretaker Clemen Raksam said visitors had been warned against venturing into remote hills and forest areas. He contacted police after learning about the robbery and visited the scene.
Jhenaigati Police Station Officer-in-Charge SM Nur Mohammad said police launched an immediate search operation but the suspects had fled into the remote hills.
Police personnel remain deployed at the tourist centre, he said, adding that further legal action would be taken if the victims filed a formal complaint.
Sherpur Deputy Commissioner Farida Yasmin said the incident occurred outside the designated tourist area despite warnings from locals. She said she had instructed the upazila nirbahi officer and the police to take necessary action.

item.title: Titumir College students vandalize ‘Durbin Bangla’ restaurant over food delay
item.description:
A group of students from Government Titumir College attacked and vandalized a restaurant in Mohakhali, Dhaka, on Thursday night following an argument over a delay in serving food.
The incident took place at Durobin Bangla restaurant following a verbal altercation and physical scuffle between the students and restaurant staff.
According to police, several students of the college ordered food at the restaurant on Thursday night. An argument broke out with the restaurant authorities over the delay in serving their order.
As the situation escalated, the restaurant manager was harassed, and a physical altercation took place between the 2 sides.
A short while later, several more students from the same college gathered at the restaurant, entered the premises and carried out an attack and vandalism.
Furniture and other items inside the restaurant were damaged, causing panic among customers.
After a video of the vandalism circulated on social media, police went to the scene upon receiving information about the incident and brought the situation under control.
On Friday, Banani police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Salahuddin said an argument and physical altercation had taken place between the students and restaurant authorities over a food order.
He said the students later called more of their fellow students to the restaurant and vandalized the premises.
No written complaint has so far been filed by the restaurant authorities at the police station, and no case has been registered in connection with the incident, he added.

item.title: Raozan Islamic Front leader gets death threat over extortion money
item.description:
Miscreants have threatened to kill Maulana Ilyas Noori, president of the Raozan upazila unit of Islamic Front and a madrasa principal, in exchange for extortion money in Raozan upazila of Chittagong, which is known as a hub of criminal activity.
In this incident, the victim has filed a general diary (GD) with Raozan police station seeking security for his life.
The principal, Maulana Ilyas Noori, who received threats over a mobile phone demanding extortion money, is the president of the Raozan upazila unit of Islamic Front. Besides, he is serving as the principal of Rangunia Betagi Rahmania Madrasa. In the last national parliamentary election, he contested from the Chittagong-6 (Raozan) constituency as the nominated candidate of the Brihattar Sunni Oikya Jote with the candle symbol and received 26,696 votes.
Regarding this, the victim principal Ilyas Noori told Dhaka Tribune: “On Thursday afternoon, while I was praying, a call came to my phone. After finishing the prayer, I received another call from the same number. The person on the other end said, “You will pay extortion money to run the boys, otherwise, wherever we find you, we will shoot and kill you.” I said that I am not a wealthy person and work at a madrasa. Then he said that he knew whether I had money or not. I would have to give them the money.”
He said: “The person on the other end of the mobile phone demanded extortion money in the name of a top miscreant of Raozan. After 10 minutes, another call came from the same number, saying, ‘Have you sent the extortion money? Send it quickly. I called again to save you. Otherwise, you will have to be killed. You have seen how many people we have killed. We will shoot and kill you too. I swear, I will kill you.’”
Ilyas Noori said: “At one point, I told him, if you want to kill me, then kill me. I do not have any money. I will not be able to pay extortion money. Saying this, I disconnected the call.”
Following this incident, Ilyas Noori, who received threats demanding extortion money, filed a written general diary at Raozan police station on Thursday night.
In the general diary, he mentioned that multiple calls were made to Ilyas Noori’s personal mobile phone from the number 01350-565309 from 1:06pm on Thursday. Later, when he called back the number at around 1:10pm, an unidentified person on the other end demanded a large sum of money from him to manage his followers. At the same time, he set a deadline for paying the demanded money by that evening. Otherwise, he threatened to kill him and cause serious harm.
The complaint further stated that later, he was harassed through multiple calls from the same number. He expressed concerns that he and his family members could be harmed at any time over his political activities. Mentioning the insecurity of himself and his family, Ilyas Noori requested the identification of the user of the mobile number concerned and legal action against him.
In this regard, Raozan police station Officer-in-Charge Saiful Islam said: “I have learned about the threats made against a person named Ilyas Noori. He has filed a general diary at the police station. Necessary measures are being taken in this regard.”
It is worth mentioning that after the change of power on August 5, 2024, 27 people have been victims of murder in Raozan upazila. Among them, at least 22 people were killed over establishing party dominance and shares of extortion money.
Currently, incidents of extortion in this upazila have increased at an alarming rate over the past few months. There are allegations that miscreants who had been in hiding in the country and abroad for a long time have returned to the area and have been carrying out these extortion demands.

item.title: PM likely to unveil tourism master plan next month
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is expected to unveil Bangladesh's long-awaited National Tourism Master Plan in December, paving the way for implementing a comprehensive development strategy covering nearly 1,500 tourism attractions from January next year.
Bangladesh Tourism Board (BTB) Chief Executive Officer Barrister Mutasim Billah Faruqui disclosed the development, saying the government was preparing to launch the master plan during the proposed Bangladesh Festival in Dhaka.
The five-day festival is tentatively scheduled for December 27-31, although the final program and the Prime Minister's participation are yet to be officially confirmed.
"We expect to submit the master plan to the ministry in the first week of December. If we can complete the finalization process and secure approval from the National Tourism Council, we aim to begin implementation in January," Faruqui said.
He said the BTB expected to receive the reviewed master plan from the review committee by November 30 before forwarding it to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism for further approval.
The BTB chief expressed optimism that the remaining formalities could be completed in time for the prime minister to formally unveil the document at the Bangladesh Festival.
The proposed announcement would mark a major milestone for Bangladesh's tourism industry, which has been awaiting a comprehensive national development blueprint since the master plan initiative began in 2019.
The process suffered repeated delays due to the COVID-19 pandemic, administrative complications and subsequent reviews during the past regimes.
According to the executive summary of the National Tourism Master Plan, the document outlines a long-term development roadmap for 2024-2041, aiming to transform Bangladesh into a competitive, sustainable tourism destination.
The plan identifies approximately 1,498 tourism resources across the country's eight administrative divisions and proposes coordinated development of infrastructure, tourism products, destination management, marketing and human resources.
It sets ambitious targets of attracting 5.58 million tourists and generating 21.94 million employment opportunities by 2041.
The blueprint proposes developing beach, ecotourism, cultural, heritage, religious, adventure, riverine, rural, cruise and meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) tourism.
It also recommends introducing electronic visas, improving tourist safety, strengthening destination management and expanding public-private partnerships to attract investment.
A major recommendation is to strengthen tourism institutions through regional training centers, destination management organizations and dedicated tourism development bodies.
Faruqui said the government intended to begin implementing priority activities from January 2027, subject to the necessary approvals.
He stressed that implementing the master plan would go beyond constructing hotels, resorts and other physical infrastructure.
"Our objective is to start implementing the activities outlined in the master plan from January," he said.
Initial activities could include destination promotion, consultations with tourism businesses, community engagement and coordination among government agencies and private-sector stakeholders.
The master plan also proposes an implementation framework identifying responsible institutions, financing options, project priorities and monitoring mechanisms.
It recommends early priority projects, investment incentives and public-private partnerships to accelerate tourism development.
Earlier, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman told parliament that the government is preparing a comprehensive tourism master plan to make tourism a major contributor to economic growth, employment generation and poverty reduction.
He said the government had identified tourism as a priority sector and would implement development projects in phases under the master plan.
The prime minister also outlined plans to develop international-standard hotels and tourism facilities on Bangladesh Parjatan Corporation-owned land in Cox's Bazar, Sylhet and Khulna.
In Cox's Bazar, the government has identified 132.44 acres of land for tourism development under public-private partnership arrangements.
A modern tourism training institute is also being developed at the Motel Laboni compound to strengthen the country's hospitality workforce.
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat subsequently told parliament that the government was finalizing an integrated master plan covering approximately 1,498 tourism sites.
He said work had also begun on formulating the National Tourism Policy 2026, alongside initiatives to promote community-based tourism, strengthen tourist security and improve tourism-sector data.
Tourism industry stakeholders have repeatedly called for the master plan's early implementation, stressing that Bangladesh's tourism potential cannot be fully realized without coordinated investment, professional destination management and improved visitor services.
Tour Operators Association of Bangladesh (TOAB) President Mohammed Hanif. has emphasized stronger tourism institutions, professional training and policy support.
Former TOAB President Md Rafeuzzaman has advocated improving visitor experiences and service quality alongside infrastructure development.
Pacific Asia Travel Association (PATA) Bangladesh Chapter Secretary General Taufiq Rahman has also stressed private-sector participation, effective destination management and coordinated implementation.
He said the master plan should place considerable emphasis on community participation, environmental sustainability, tourism marketing and improved connectivity.

item.title: Palli Bidyut: No evidence of short circuit at MP Nusrat’s house
item.description:
Kushtia Palli Bidyut Samity has found no evidence of an electrical short circuit in the fire that damaged the village home of reserved-seat MP and National Citizen Party (NCP) leader Nusrat Tabassum in Daulatpur Upazila.
The findings came after officials examined electrical wires, the meter and fuses recovered from the house.
Tojammel Haque, assistant general manager (operations and maintenance) of the samity’s Pragpur Sub-Zonal Office, confirmed the findings on Friday afternoon.
He said the power distribution line remained intact and showed no signs of a short circuit.
Following a call to the complaint centre, electricity supply to the house was immediately disconnected. Two linemen later visited the site and recovered the wires and meter for examination, he said.
Although the meter’s outer casing was damaged by the fire, its internal circuit showed no evidence of a short circuit. The cartridge fuses in the main switch were also intact, Tojammel said, adding that they would normally have blown had a short circuit occurred.
He also said the house had standard-rated fuses and no higher-rated fuses had been installed.
Based on these findings, officials found no evidence linking the fire to an electrical fault. However, the actual cause of the incident remains unknown.
Police, Fire Service and Civil Defence, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), the civil administration and other agencies are investigating the incident.
Delwar Hossain, additional superintendent of police (Bheramara Circle), said investigators had yet to determine how the fire started.
Several agencies, including the fire service and the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), are conducting investigations, and a decision will be made based on their findings, he said.
The fire broke out around 11:45pm on Wednesday at Nusrat’s family home in Baguayan village under the Dangmorka area of Daulatpur, damaging several rooms.
On Thursday night, the MP filed a case with Daulatpur Police Station, accusing unidentified people of attempting to kill her parents and other family members by setting fire to the house and causing an explosion.

item.title: Bangladesh pavilion draws attention on COP31 opening day in Türkiye
item.description:
The Bangladesh Pavilion witnessed an unusually vibrant and packed atmosphere on the opening day of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, marking a significant shift from previous years when the country's national pavilion often received limited attention and engagement during the global climate summit.
Under the leadership of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Bangladesh has introduced several significant changes to its national pavilion this year, many of which represent firsts for the country's participation in the COP Blue Zone.
With a renewed focus on public engagement, innovation and international visibility, the pavilion features interactive wall designs, souvenir distribution and immersive virtual reality (VR) experiences.
Visitors experienced the realities faced by aid workers in flood-affected communities, alongside a striking virtual journey highlighting the contrast between the natural beauty of Cox's Bazar and the growing environmental challenges posed by pollution.
This year's pavilion is centred on showcasing Bangladesh's climate strategies, national action plans and ongoing resilience initiatives, while positioning the country as an attractive destination for investment in climate adaptation, environmental protection and sustainable development.
Another notable milestone this year is the introduction of private-sector support for the Bangladesh Pavilion's activities and development.
MGH Group and Eastern Bank PLC have joined as partners, contributing to the pavilion's beautification, visitor engagement activities, souvenir distribution and immersive VR experiences.
Perhaps one of the most significant developments has been the Ministry's decision to actively involve youth organizations in the planning, decision-making and management of the pavilion. Representatives from youth-led organizations, including Footsteps, Go UP Foundation and Youth4NDCs, have played an instrumental role in enhancing visitor engagement and managing pavilion activities.
Their involvement has brought fresh perspectives, creativity and energy to the national pavilion, helping it capture considerable attention on the opening day.
The Bangladesh Pavilion was formally inaugurated by Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo and State Minister Dr. Shaikh Faridul Islam on the opening day of COP31.
In another historic development, Bangladesh is participating with two national pavilions at COP31 for the first time.
Alongside the MoEFCC-led pavilion in the Blue Zone, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is hosting a separate pavilion in the Green Zone, showcasing Bangladesh's traditional and innovative jute products to an international audience.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is also scheduled to join the Bangladesh delegation at COP31 on 11 November, further underscoring the country's commitment to advancing its climate diplomacy and international engagement.
The 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) is taking place in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026.
The annual summit brings together world leaders, policymakers, climate experts, civil society organizations and private-sector representatives to negotiate global climate action, including the mobilization of climate finance and resources to address the escalating impacts of climate change.
With a renewed vision, stronger partnerships and meaningful youth participation, the Bangladesh Pavilion at COP31 is emerging as an important platform for showcasing the country's climate leadership, resilience, innovation and investment opportunities to the world.

item.title: Father, twin daughters found dead at in-laws’ home in Chittagong
item.description:
A man and his seven-month-old twin daughters were found dead at his in-laws’ house in Banshkhali upazila of Chittagong on Friday.
The deceased were identified as Jahed Hossain, 50, and his twin daughters, Jarin and Jasia. Jahed was found hanging inside a room, while the bodies of the two infants were recovered from the floor beside the bed.
Police have taken Jahed’s wife, mother-in-law and sister-in-law into custody for questioning over their suspected involvement in the incident.
The incident occurred between noon and 3pm on Friday at Mawlar Para in Madhyam Puichhari area of Puichhari Union.
Police initially suspect that the infants were smothered with pillows.
Jahed was the son of the late Badiul Alam, former acting chairman of Banshkhali Upazila Parishad.
Local Union Parishad member Saddam Hossain Manik said Jahed’s ancestral home was in Chambal village, but he had been living at his in-laws’ house for the past one and a half years.
Jahed’s wife, Afia Begum, said she and her mother had gone to a mosque in Villager Para to fulfil a religious vow. As Jahed had offered to look after the children, she prepared milk for them before leaving.
She said she later tried calling him but received no response. When she returned home in the afternoon, she found both the main gate and the room locked.
Mizanur Rahman, an official at the Banshkhali Fire Service Station, said firefighters cut through the room’s partition after finding it locked from the inside. They recovered Jahed’s hanging body and the bodies of the two infants from the floor beside the bed.
Banshkhali Police Station Officer-in-Charge Robiul Haque said police rushed to the scene after receiving information and recovered all three bodies.
He said family disputes or mental distress might have led to the incident, although the actual cause remained unclear.
The bodies were sent to the morgue of Chittagong Medical College Hospital for autopsies, he added.
Assistant Superintendent of Police (Anwara Circle) Mamudul Hasan said a handwritten note was recovered from the scene, stating that Jahed was owed Tk2 lakh by his mother-in-law. Police are verifying whether he wrote the note.
He said the bodies were recovered with the help of local residents and that the autopsy process was underway.
The exact circumstances surrounding the deaths are being investigated, and legal action will be taken accordingly, he added.

item.title: NCP MP Mahmuda Mitu alleges receiving death threats for 7 days
item.description:
National Citizen Party (NCP) political council member and Member of Parliament Mahmuda Alam Mitu has alleged that she has been receiving death threats over the phone and WhatsApp for the past 7 days. She made the allegation in a post on her verified Facebook account on Friday evening.
In the post, she wrote: “I became extremely emotional in parliament on Thursday, and at one point, I also lost my temper. This is because this parliament stands on the blood of hundreds of martyrs, the sacrifices of the injured, and the sacrifices of July coordinators like Hannan Masud and one-point demand proclaimer like Nahid Islam. Yet, unable to engage with them in arguments, they are being addressed informally and insulted as ‘ill-mannered’ right inside parliament! Whenever someone cannot win an argument, they are labelled ill-mannered.”
She further wrote: “When Hannan was repeatedly being told ‘Sit down’ and called ‘ill-mannered’, I was shouting that we are the ones who receive death threats and whose houses are set on fire. How can people who operate through alliances understand how much courage it takes to engage in politics while leaving the security of one's parents, children and oneself uncertain?”
MP Mitu further said she had been receiving death threats directly over the phone and WhatsApp for the past 7 days. She had received such threats before as well.
She added that even if she spoke about these matters, attempts might be made to downplay them, as in the case of Nusrat. Hadi had said: “Until bullets hit our necks and heads, no one will feel concerned!”

item.title: Speaker: Women should get chance to contest 100 seats directly
item.description:
Women should have the opportunity to secure 100 parliamentary seats through direct elections instead of the existing reserved-seat system, Speaker Major (retd) Hafiz Uddin Ahmed Bir Bikram has said.
He made the remarks while addressing the centenary celebration of Barisal Government Girls’ High School as the chief guest on Friday afternoon.
“Genuine political empowerment of women requires giving them the opportunity to contest direct elections. There should be provisions for women to be elected to 100 parliamentary seats through direct voting. Women are in no way behind,” Hafiz Uddin Ahmed said.
Highlighting the contribution of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia to female education, the speaker said she had introduced free education for girls up to the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) level.
He also said he would discuss with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman the possibility of extending free education for girls up to the bachelor's degree level.
Highlighting the school's historical significance, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed said Barisal Government Girls’ High School had served as the first secretariat of the Liberation War and played an important role in the country's struggle for independence.
“History will remember the institution's contribution to the Liberation War,” he said.
Addressing the school's former and current students, he said: “The pull of one's roots is irresistible. Many distinguished students have graduated from this institution. The school has given you so much, and now it is your turn to give something back.”
He urged former students to support those who were unable to continue their education due to financial constraints.
Recalling his school days, the speaker said childhood memories of school life were unforgettable. He said he had studied at Barisal Zilla School and recalled that there were no gatherings in front of the girls' school at the time, adding that the social environment might have been different back then.
The two-day centenary celebration was chaired by Barisal City Corporation Administrator and the school's former student Bilkis Akter Jahan Shirin.
Barisal-5 MP Mujibur Rahman Sarwar, along with former and current students of the school, attended the programme.
Former student and veteran teacher Jahanara Begum, Professor Shah Sajeda, Shamima Masud Munni and others also spoke at the event.

item.title: ULAB crowned ABG University Cup Cricket 2026 champions
item.description:
University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) clinched the ABG University Cup 2026 Cricket Tournament title, defeating Sonargaon University by 53 runs in the final at the Bashundhara Cricket Stadium.
Batting first, ULAB posted an imposing 205 for two, powered by a magnificent unbeaten century from Farhan Jani. In reply, Sonargaon University managed 152 for nine, handing ULAB a convincing victory and the championship trophy.
ULAB's Farhan Shovon was named Player of the Final for his outstanding performance, while the university dominated the individual awards. Rakib claimed the Best Bowler award, Zakirul Gem was named Best Batsman as well as Player of the Tournament.
The champions also received prize money of Tk 10 lakh.
A total of 10 private universities participated in the tournament, including ULAB, Sonargaon University, Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB), North South University (NSU), BRAC University, Daffodil International University, Scholars University, Fareast University, United International University (UIU) and American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB).
ULAB's title-winning campaign was highlighted by a commanding batting display in the final and a disciplined bowling effort that kept Sonargaon well below the target.

item.title: A collective failure
item.description:
The tragic loss of at least 20 young lives to suicide following the publication of this year’s SSC and HSC examination results -- including nine deaths within just ten days of the recent HSC announcement -- is a devastating indictment of our society.
Worse still, given the pervasive stigma surrounding mental health and self-harm across the country, these reported figures likely represent only a fraction of the true toll.
When teenagers choose to end their lives over academic scores, it exposes a profound moral and institutional collapse. That we live in a society where exam grades are treated as the sole determinant of human worth is a horrifying reality.
For decades, parents, educators, and communities have conditioned students to believe that falling short of a coveted GPA-5 or failing a board examination equates to absolute ruin. The relentless cycle of parental comparisons, social humiliation, and rigid academic expectations leaves vulnerable young minds isolated and terrified of disappointing their families.
When an examination hall becomes a matter of life and death, the entire pedagogical and social framework has fundamentally broken down. No board certificate is worth a single child's life, yet our culture continues to weaponize academic performance against the emotional well-being of our children.
This crisis demands immediate, structural intervention from both the state and society. We need accessible, confidential psychological counseling services in our educational institutions -- not as a formality, but as an active support network operating before and after exam seasons. Simultaneously, we must also expand emergency crisis helplines and train teachers to recognize early signs of acute distress and isolation.
Beyond policy, families must replace interrogation and shame with empathy and understanding, reassuring their children that academic setbacks are temporary obstacles, not life sentences.
If we continue to prioritize grades over emotional survival, these preventable tragedies will remain an annual stain on our national conscience. We must act now to protect our youth before another promising life is lost to despair.

item.title: Road crash involving bus, container truck kills 23 in India
item.description:
A head-on collision between a container truck and a passenger bus killed at least 23 people, including three children, in eastern India on Friday, a police official told AFP.
The crash took place on a highway bordering Kaziranga National Park in the northeastern state of Assam.
The road is a designated animal corridor, where strict speed limits are in place.
“The total number of casualties is 23,” said Swapneel Deka, the local district police chief.
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said he was “deeply distressed by the tragic accident.”
“The scale of this loss has shaken all of us, and my heart goes out to every family that has lost a loved one,” Sarma said on X.
India, with a population of 1.4 billion, recorded more than 183,000 road traffic deaths in 2025, or over 500 a day, according to the roads ministry.
Many accidents are linked to inadequate road infrastructure, poorly maintained vehicles and exhausted drivers, according to official data.

item.title: New bridge ends years of suffering in Rangamati
item.description:
A newly constructed bridge connecting Rangamati Central Cemetery to the Police Hospital has ended years of suffering for local residents, making daily travel significantly easier for thousands of people.
Previously, residents had to wait for boats to cross the canal or take a long detour that could take 20 to 30 minutes. Now, they can reach their destinations in just five to seven minutes. The bridge has improved connectivity for more than 200 families, benefiting students, patients and other residents.
According to the Chittagong Hill Tracts Development Board, the bridge was constructed under a project covering the 2021-2026 period. The 130-metre-long and 3.6-metre-wide structure was built at a cost of around Tk4.95 crore.
Several important institutions, including Rangamati Government High School, the Police Hospital, the Old Police Lines and Police Lines Government Primary School, are located near the bridge. Hundreds of people use it daily.
A recent visit to the area found that the bridge has brought considerable relief, particularly to residents of the Old Police Lines, the Police Hospital and neighbouring areas. It has also become a popular spot for locals and visitors, especially in the afternoon.
Mohammad Naim, a student of Rangamati Government High School, said the bridge had significantly reduced travel time, making it easier for students to commute.
Local resident Zainal Abedin said reaching home previously took 20 to 30 minutes on foot, but the journey now required much less time.
Kajol Begum, a resident of the Police Lines area, said people previously had to wait for boats at the ghat. The bridge had saved valuable time for children going to school and residents travelling to the market.
Tarikul Islam Tanmoy, a resident near the Police Hospital, said finding a boat at night was particularly difficult. Now, people could reach their destinations within five to seven minutes.
Joni Das, a resident of the Police Lines area, has called for a connecting road to allow vehicles from different parts of the town to reach the bridge directly.
Majhi Hossain, who has lived in the area for 19 years, said crossing the canal had been particularly difficult before the bridge was built. Boats were unavailable after 9 pm, creating serious problems during medical emergencies and when transporting deceased residents to the cemetery. He said the bridge had ended years of suffering.
Chittagong Hill Tracts Development Board Executive Engineer Tushit Chakma said the project was implemented to improve Rangamati municipality's communication network. He said the bridge had eased students' journeys to school and was contributing to the overall development of the area.

item.title: Bangladesh prepares to extract gas from Inani
item.description:
Bangladesh has started preparations to extract natural gas from Inani in Ukhiya upazila of Cox’s Bazar, where a gas-fuelled fire has been burning for 18 days following a deep tube-well drilling operation.
The Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company (Bapex) began transporting heavy machinery, pipes and drilling equipment to the site yesterday morning, raising expectations that controlled drilling and technical operations could start soon.
Ukhiya Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Panna Akter said authorities had been monitoring the situation since the fire broke out. Section 144 was imposed to ensure public safety and prevent potential hazards, including explosions and landslides. Fire Service personnel and law enforcement agencies have also been deployed.
She said a high-level expert team was assessing the gas pressure and flow, geological structure and safety requirements for extraction.
Bapex geologist Nasir Uddin said prolonged monitoring showed that gas pressure and flow remained stable. "Decisions have been taken in principle on how to control the fire safely and proceed towards commercial gas extraction," he said.
Local traders Jasim Uddin, Mohammad Ali and Mir Ahmed said heavy equipment had been arriving at the site since yesterday morning. They expressed hope that drilling operations would begin soon, potentially paving the way for Inani to become the country's 31st gas field.
Experts believe the sustained gas flow and pressure could indicate substantial underground reserves rather than a small gas pocket. However, geological surveys, seismic studies and further tests are needed to determine the size and commercial viability of the deposit.
Bangladesh has 30 discovered gas fields, around 20 of which are producing commercially. If sufficient reserves are confirmed and commercial extraction proves viable, Inani would become the country's 31st gas field, potentially strengthening energy security and reducing dependence on imports.
Gas first emerged and caught fire on October 27 during the drilling of a deep tube well at Chhoto Inani in Jaliapalong union of Ukhiya upazila. The gas was released from a depth of around 1,000 feet.
